messages.subject: c.cross problem, possibly bug?
parts:
Dear Karl,

I'm experiencing an error when trying to merge a F2 cross object and a BC cross object. They have exactly the same chromosomes, markers, etc. I think it's a bug and I've detailed it below but I wanted to check that I'm not doing something wrong.

I also have a few questions: 
1) given that my F2 and BC crosses are genotyped at exactly the same locations, I could just concatenate my genotype and phenotype files before reading them into R/qtl. How would that affect my results compared to using c.cross? 
2) Also, with the output from c.cross, do I need to add one of the new phenotype columns (cross1, cross2, cross, for example) as a covariate or is the batch/cross type covariate automatically inputted somehow?

Thank you,
Andrew

The error message reads:

Error in dimnames(geno[[j]]$prob) <- dimnames(x$geno[[j]]$prob) : 
  length of 'dimnames' [1] not equal to array extent

I believe this is caused by a bug in util.R at line 1788, when R/qtl is trying to name the concatenated genotype array. I believe you could fix it by replacing line 1788 with the following: 
dimnames(geno[[j]]$prob)[[1]] <- character(length = sum(n.ind))
dimnames(geno[[j]]$prob)[[2]] <- dimnames(args[[wh]]$geno[[j]]$prob)[[2]]
dimnames(geno[[j]]$prob)[[3]] <- dimnames(args[[wh]]$geno[[j]]$prob)[[3]]
And then add on (what was previously) line 1793:
dimnames(geno[[j]]$prob)[[1]][wh] = dimnames(args[[i]]$geno[[j]]$prob)[[1]]

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] c.cross problem, possibly bug?
parts:
Thanks; I'll look into the c.cross problem. Can you say more about the case where the problem arose, because I've not seen this before.
If you could provide an example, that would be helpful.

Regarding the output of c.cross, you will have to specify covariates in scanone etc; nothing is done automatically.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] c.cross problem, possibly bug?
parts:
Thanks for your response. This is a bit embarrassing... Upon trying to create a small example file to play with, I am unable to recapitulate my error. I am using MSG, so I used read.cross.msg to read in the genotype probabilities and I'm guessing this may be causing the merging problem. 

When I first tried this, I read in the BC1 and F2 data separately, then merged them. However, this resulted in my BC1 genotypes being switched to heterozygous. I think this is because read.cross.msg somehow read in the BC1 genotypes "backwards" and R/qtl thought I had invalid genotypes for a backcross. (I though had fixed this problem, but I guess not completely)

I'm wondering if it's possible to entirely circumvent this problem. Since I ran MSG on the BC1 and F2 individuals all together, all the individuals' genotypes are in a single file with the same markers and everything. Is there a difference between reading the BC1 and F2 in separately and then merging them, as opposed to reading in the combined genotype probabilities and then setting cross$pheno$crosstype?

Thank you,
Andrew

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] c.cross problem, possibly bug?
parts:
No worries.

It seems like you should be able to read the merged cross. For QTL analysis with scanone() etc, it's going to ignore any genotypes and just use the genotype probabilities.

karl
